newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed down, giving up most of Friday's U.S. payrolls-inspired gains as profit-taking in Bunds weighed heavily and investors anxious about a lack of clear new direction took to the sidelines.
"It's been very quiet, with everybody a little bit anxious," one Amsterdam dealer said. "Before you take a view now you have to sit back a while to think about it."

Dutch bonds slid into the close as Bunds neared session lows, but dealers said the underlying outlook was still broadly positive with the thin supply of paper resulting from the tight Dutch funding calender expected to provide support.
The yield discount to Germany moved out slightly, with the 10-year spread widening to around 12 basis points, reversing some of the notable underperformance by Guilders on Friday.
Analysts said the discount to Bunds looked to be fairly stable at around these levels and the discount might well be maintained through the year.

Friday's narrowing from 14 basis points down to nine during the reaction after the U.S. payrolls figure could partly be attributed to greater liquidity in the German market, one dealer said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
